code: centre <- function(r) {   cbind(rowMeans(matrix(r$P[t(r$T), 1], ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)),         rowMeans(matrix(r$P[t(r$T), 2], ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE))) } inside_ring <- function(p, ring) {   j <- nrow(ring); inside <- rep(FALSE, nrow(p))   for (i in seq_len(nrow(ring))) {     cross <- ((ring[i, 2] > p[, 2]) != (ring[j, 2] > p[, 2])) &       (p[, 1] < (ring[j, 1] - ring[i, 1]) * (p[, 2] - ring[i, 2]) /          (ring[j, 2] - ring[i, 2]) + ring[i, 1])     inside <- xor(inside, cross); j <- i   }   inside } p <- centre(r) truth <- sapply(1:4, function(f) {   inside <- rep(FALSE, nrow(p))   for (ring in rings) if (ring$feature == f) inside <- xor(inside, inside_ring(p, ring$xy))   inside }) all((w != 0) == truth) #> [1] TRUE

title: Constrained Delaunay Triangulation with Refinement
text: Vertices segments , vertices triangles . square square hole: two closed rings segments. depth number constraint boundaries crossed way outside: 0 outside everything, nested rings odd inside, even hole. default triangles outside outermost boundary already dropped (erase = "outer", Triangle’s -p ); erase = "holes" also drops even depths.
code: library(cdtr) x <- c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75, 0.25) y <- c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0.25, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75) s0 <- 1:8; s1 <- c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5) r <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1) str(r[c("P", "T", "S", "depth")]) #> List of 4 #>  $ P    : num [1:8, 1:2] 0 1 1 0 0.25 0.75 0.75 0.25 0 0 ... #>  $ T    : int [1:10, 1:3] 8 6 8 7 6 5 8 6 2 2 ... #>  $ S    : int [1:8, 1:2] 1 3 1 5 6 2 7 5 2 4 ... #>  $ depth: int [1:10] 2 1 1 1 2 1 1 1 1 1 plot_mesh <- function(m, main = "") {   e <- cdt_edges(m)   plot(m$P, asp = 1, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", pch = ".", main = main)   segments(m$P[e[, 1], 1], m$P[e[, 1], 2], m$P[e[, 2], 1], m$P[e[, 2], 2], col = "grey50")   segments(m$P[m$S[, 1], 1], m$P[m$S[, 1], 2], m$P[m$S[, 2], 1], m$P[m$S[, 2], 2], lwd = 2) } op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 2, 0.5)) plot_mesh(r, "constrained") plot_mesh(cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1, max_area = 0.01), "max_area = 0.01") plot_mesh(cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1, max_area = 0.01, min_angle = 25, erase = "holes"),           "+ min_angle = 25, holes erased") par(op)

title: Locate points in a triangle mesh — cdt_locate
code: P <- cbind(c(0, 1, 1, 0), c(0, 0, 1, 1)) T <- rbind(c(1, 2, 3), c(1, 3, 4)) ## (0.5, 0.5) is on the shared diagonal: the lower triangle id wins cdt_locate(P, T, xq = c(0.75, 0.25, 0.5, 2), yq = c(0.25, 0.75, 0.5, 2)) #> [1]  1  2  1 NA  ## the weights of each triangle's vertices loc <- cdt_locate(P, T, xq = c(0.75, 0.25, 0.5), yq = c(0.25, 0.75, 0.5),                   barycentric = TRUE) loc #>   triangle   b1   b2   b3 #> 1        1 0.25 0.50 0.25 #> 2        2 0.25 0.25 0.50 #> 3        1 0.50 0.00 0.50 ## a value known at the vertices, interpolated with those weights z <- c(0, 10, 20, 10) rowSums(as.matrix(loc[c("b1", "b2", "b3")]) * matrix(z[T[loc$triangle, ]], ncol = 3)) #> [1] 10 10 10

code: ## unit square with a square hole: two closed rings of 4 vertices x <- c(0, 1, 1, 0, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75, 0.25) y <- c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0.25, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75) s0 <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8) s1 <- c(2, 3, 4, 1, 6, 7, 8, 5)  ## constrained triangulation, hole triangles kept with even depth r <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1) table(r$depth) #>  #> 1 2  #> 8 2   ## drop the hole and refine by area and minimum angle r2 <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1, erase = "holes",                       max_area = 0.005, min_angle = 25) table(r2$origin) #>  #>    input crossing  steiner  #>        8        0      112  plot(r2$P, asp = 1, pch = ".") polygon(r2$P[t(cbind(r2$T, NA)), ], col = "grey90")   ## erase the region around a point instead (like RTriangle's pslg H) r5 <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1, holes = cbind(0.5, 0.5)) table(r5$depth) #>  #> 1  #> 8   ## which input segments make up each fixed edge r4 <- cdt_triangulate(x, y, s0, s1, max_area = 0.05, edge_sources = TRUE) head(r4$edge_sources) #>   edge segment forward #> 1    1       1   FALSE #> 2    2       6    TRUE #> 3    3       3   FALSE #> 4    4       4    TRUE #> 5    5       4   FALSE #> 6    6       3    TRUE  ## points only: Delaunay triangulation of the convex hull set.seed(1) r3 <- cdt_triangulate(runif(30), runif(30)) nrow(r3$T) #> [1] 51

code: ## two overlapping squares, in a frame (feature 0) sq <- function(x0, y0, x1, y1) rbind(c(x0, y0), c(x1, y0), c(x1, y1), c(x0, y1)) rings <- list(sq(0, 0, 2, 2), sq(1, 1, 3, 3), sq(-1, -1, 4, 4)) feature <- c(1, 2, 0) n <- vapply(rings, nrow, 1L) first <- cumsum(c(0L, n[-length(n)])) xy <- do.call(rbind, rings) s0 <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(n), function(k) first[k] + 1:4)) s1 <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(n), function(k) first[k] + c(2:4, 1L))) r <- cdt_triangulate(xy[, 1], xy[, 2], s0, s1, max_area = 0.5,                      edge_sources = TRUE) w <- cdt_winding(r, owner = rep(feature, n), outside = c(-0.5, -0.5)) ## triangles by the features covering them table(feature_1 = w[, 1], feature_2 = w[, 2]) #>          feature_2 #> feature_1  0  1 #>         0 48  6 #>         1  6  2

title: cdtr 0.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-10-21 First release. cdt_triangulate() wraps ‘CDT’ C++ library constrained conforming Delaunay triangulation, Ruppert refinement maximum area minimum angle, resolution crossing constraints, per-triangle topological region depth.
